## How and Why I Used AI

- **Claude:** planning the assignment, preparing a line-by-line note template
  for Murrell's chapter 1 code, checking my answers to the questions in those
  notes, extracting the 2024 subset of the Happy Planet Index workbook,
  scaffolding this page, and reviewing the finished draft.
- **Codex:** turning my notes into an English draft and writing the R plotting
  examples and figure captions from that scaffold.
- **Why:** to catch up after starting the course late, to work with unfamiliar
  tooling (Quarto rendering, base R graphics), and to express my observations
  in English, which is not my first language.
- **What is my own:** the line-by-line runs of the chapter 1 code and the
  observations recorded in my notes, the choice of 2024, the decision about
  which sections of the chapter to run and which to skip, and the judgement
  that a bar chart would serve the regional counts better than a pie chart.

## Conversation Log — Claude

### 1. Understanding what Assignment 2 asks for

> **Me:** 我覺得差不多要準備做 Assignment 2，考試準備到一個段落了。
>
> *(I think it is about time to start Assignment 2; my exam preparation has reached a stopping point.)*

**Claude:** Read the handout and broke it into four tasks: run Murrell's
chapter 1 code line by line, exercise twelve plotting functions on my own data
with one figure and one sentence each, use the Happy Planet Index filtered to a
single year, and post the figures **with the code that produced them**.
Estimated four to six hours and suggested splitting it over two days.

### 2. Getting the chapter 1 code

> **Me:** *(Shared the chapter 1 figure gallery page and reported that `murrell01.R` was not on Teams.)*

**Claude:** The gallery links to separate `.R` files rather than one script, and
Claude's own network could not reach the site. It wrote an R script that reads
the chapter page from my machine, extracts every `.R` link, downloads them, and
concatenates them into a single `murrell01.R`. The first attempt found nothing
because the page uses uppercase `HREF`; after Claude made the pattern
case-insensitive, all 14 files downloaded (1,295 lines).

> **Me:** *(Reported `system error 32` when opening the file.)*

**Claude:** Diagnosed it as a file connection left open by the failed first run
(`close(con)` never executed), and pointed out that this is the same discipline
as `png()` needing `dev.off()`. `closeAllConnections()` or restarting R fixed it.

>

::: {.callout-note}
## 4. Checking my answers (most relevant)

> **Me:** *(Submitted my answers to the six questions.)*

**Claude:** Confirmed two answers and corrected three:

- **`text()` before `plot()`**: in a fresh session this is an *error*
  (`plot.new has not been called yet`); I had seen "the text does not appear"
  only because an old plot was still on the device.
- **What `plot()` does**: it is `plot.new()` + `plot.window()` + drawing the
  data + `axis(1)` + `axis(2)` + `box()` + `title()`; my answer covered only
  the first step.
- **`freq = FALSE`**: I had the direction backwards. On a count scale the
  density curve is compressed against the axis, because counts reach the teens
  while the density peaks near 0.4.
- **`boxplot(add = TRUE)`**: I said it still counted as high-level because it
  clears the plot. It does **not** clear the plot; with `add = TRUE` it behaves
  as a low-level call, which is why the two sets of boxes sit side by side.
- **`midpts`**: my value was right; Claude added the reason it is needed — the
  bars are not at 1, 2, 3, 4, so the labels need the returned positions.
- **`theta` / `phi`**: rotation versus viewing elevation.

Claude also filled in the type column for all 38 rows as a check against my own
reading.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## 5. The data and the page scaffold (most relevant)

> **Me:** 好的就 2024 年吧。
>
> *(All right, let's use 2024.)*

**Claude:** Checked how complete each year is and recommended 2024, because the
GDP column is empty for 2025. Extracted the 2024 rows from the `All Data` sheet
into `hpi2024.csv` (153 countries), and translated the workbook's numeric
continent codes into region names after verifying the order against the
workbook's own `Cont data` sheet. Reported the missing values I cite on the
assignment page: life satisfaction 12, HPI 16, GDP 6, footprint 4. It also
wrote `02_export_csv.R` so the same extract is reproducible from the original
workbook, and created the skeleton of `assignment2.qmd` with the twelve chunks
and hints — including the suggestion to fit a smoothed surface for `persp()`,
since that function needs a grid rather than country rows.
:::

### 6. Reviewing the draft

> **Me:** 是這樣嗎？幫我看一下。
>
> *(Is this right? Please take a look.)*

**Claude:** Checked the page and the rendered output. Confirmed the code was
correct, including the `hpi ~ continent` formula (the data frame and the column
share a name) and the orientation of the `persp()` matrix. Asked for three
changes, which I made: naming **both** AI tools in the statement rather than
only Codex, adding Assignment 2 to the site navigation, and hiding the `str()`

twelve figures for screen readers and sharpened the `par()` caption to say that
the call draws nothing by itself.
